identity.title: Guaranteed Optimal Compositional Explanations for Neurons

problem.claim: Compute compositional explanations that describe spatial alignment between neuron receptive-field activations and concepts through logical rules.

gap.claim: Beam search restricts the state space but provides no theoretical optimality guarantee, leaving the distance from the true optimum unclear.

contributions.claim: A framework for computing guaranteed optimal compositional explanations across the state space allowed by adopted assumptions.
A decomposition of alignment factors, a search-stage alignment estimator, and an algorithm reported to achieve optimal explanations in time comparable to exhaustive beam search.
A beam-search variant guided by the proposed decomposition and heuristic, with flexibility in hyperparameters and computational resources.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors describe the framework and optimal-explanation algorithm as the first of their kind under the paper’s stated setting.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that 10–40% of explanations previously obtained with beam search are suboptimal when concepts overlap.
The authors report that their guided beam-search variant matches or improves runtime over prior methods while offering greater flexibility in hyperparameters and computational resources.

narrative_sequence.summary: Compositional explanations search logical combinations of concepts to characterize spatial alignment with neuron activations.
Because the full state space is infeasible to evaluate, existing work uses combination-structure assumptions and beam search.
Beam search lacks an optimality guarantee, so the quality gap to the true optimum is unresolved.
The paper introduces a guaranteed-optimal framework built from an alignment decomposition, a heuristic estimator, and an optimal search algorithm.
The authors report substantial beam-search suboptimality with overlapping concepts and favorable runtime for a guided variant.

source_observation.claim: The abstract pairs a decomposition of the objective with a heuristic estimator and then connects both to an optimal algorithm and a guided approximate variant.

lessons.interpretation: Separating objective structure from search guidance can support both guarantee-oriented and resource-flexible methods.
lessons.application: When proposing a combinatorial method, explicitly expose the factors driving the objective and show how the same structure guides a practical search variant.
lessons.exception: This framing may be unsuitable when the objective lacks a useful decomposition or when approximation guidance cannot preserve the desired guarantees.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the adopted assumptions, the exact guarantee, datasets or evaluation protocol, or what “comparable” and “matches or improves runtime” quantify.
The reported 10–40% suboptimality range is not contextualized by task, model, search settings, or baseline details.
